entities.summary:
Gofraid mac Sitriuc, in Old Norse Guðrøðr Sigtryggsson, was King of Dublin from 944 CE until his death in 951 CE. He was the son of Sihtric ua Ímair and a great-grandson of Ímar, founder of the Uí Ímair kindred which dominated much of the Norse-Gael and Scandinavianised parts of Britain and Ireland in the 10th century. This Uí Ímair dynasty played a crucial role in shaping the political landscape of Ireland during the Viking Age. As King of Dublin, Gofraid mac Sitriuc oversaw the construction of several major buildings, including the Dublin Cathedral, and implemented various policies to strengthen the city's economy and military.

Gofraid's reign was marked by several significant events, including the Viking invasion of England in 954 CE, which led to the establishment of the Kingdom of Dublin. He also played a key role in the negotiations between the Vikings and the Irish High King, which resulted in the signing of the Treaty of Dublin in 954 CE. This treaty established the Kingdom of Dublin as a vassal state of the Irish High King and secured a period of relative peace and stability in the region.

The legacy of Gofraid mac Sitriuc can be seen in the continued dominance of the Uí Ímair dynasty in Ireland for several centuries. His policies and achievements helped to establish Dublin as a major center of power and commerce, and his legacy continues to be felt in the modern-day city.

Gofraid mac Sitriuc's reign was marked by a series of striking events, including the Viking raid on the monastery at Clonmacnoise in 950 CE, which resulted in the destruction of the monastery and the killing of many monks. This event had a profound impact on the development of Christianity in Ireland, as it led to a renewed emphasis on the importance of monastic education and the preservation of sacred texts.
